item.text: I’m checking the new torus argument first, then I’ll trace every row family through the denominator induction and audit the earlier lemmas for any remaining chain-breaking defects.

The new L6d/Fact F argument is correct. In particular, (T1) is genuinely independent of the fixed constant term \(c\), and the shared-vertex telescope has no conditioning leakage: after summing over \(V_j\), the resulting factor is independent of \(V_{j+1}\), so the next elimination is legitimate. Fact F’s falling-factorial count is also correct in every characteristic.

I found the following defects.

1. **CRITICAL ERROR — the general O2 tables are not fully defined.**

> “under (O2) the designated terminal rows additionally carry the summand \(\kappa_1\)”

and

> “\(t := s + (\kappa_1\) distributed into designated exit rows)”

No datum specifies which terminal rows are “designated,” nor how the single mass \(\kappa_1\) is distributed when there is more than one such row. The composition datum in §2.3(iv) only assigns verdicts to the already-defined families from (ii)/(iii); it does not supply this missing O2 allocation. The degree-2 example chooses one allocation, but no general-\(e\) rule is stated.

Consequently, the promised family \(\mathfrak B_n\), its O2 entry lists \(E(e)\), and its solved \(t_\sigma\) are not determined for general \(n\). The denominator argument would tolerate any finite allocation, but the theorem is stated about a particular defined family, and that family has not actually been defined.

2. **CRITICAL ERROR — the concrete degree-3 conjunct is not verifiable from the supplied data.**

> “junction masses e.g. …; stratum masses with denominators \(q^3-1\), \(q^6-1\) and their products; final densities with denominators dividing …, e.g. \(R=\cdots\). This is (O3) at \(e=2,3\). All are elements of \(\mathcal R\).”

The claim expressly includes that the project’s concrete sealed degree-3 tables are instances of O3 and that every concrete entry satisfies the denominator condition. Section 7 supplies only example entries and a blanket assertion about the omitted entries. It does not display the complete concrete entry lists, kernels beyond the two scalar kernels, or a correspondence between all concrete rows and the seven families. Thus neither the instance-identification nor the all-entry denominator claim follows from this self-contained package.

3. **JUSTIFICATION GAP — the Newton-polygon exhaustion is only valid up to a null set as written.**

> “their disjoint union over admissible \(P\) exhausts, since every \(g\in C_e\setminus R_e\) has SOME polygon”

The definition of L6 requires a finite polygon on all of \([0,e]\), beginning at \(x_1=0\), with a finite vertex height there. But coefficients may equal zero, hence have valuation \(+\infty\). For example, a polynomial in \(C_e\setminus R_e\) may have \(a_e=0\) while another coefficient violates the \(R_e\) bounds. Its ordinary finite Newton polygon need not begin at column \(0\), and it is not represented by an L6 face-kind with \(\sum L_j=e\).

These omitted coefficient-zero loci have Haar measure zero, so the displayed mass calculations can still be accepted after assuming the required almost-everywhere exhaustion. The exact set-theoretic “complete partition” and exhaustion assertions, however, are unproved and literally false under the given finite-polygon definition.

Everything else checked successfully:

- Fact F’s Möbius formula and multiset assignment denominator \(\prod_m c_{D,m}!\) are correct.
- In (T1), normalization by the leading coefficient and rescaling by \(c/S(0)\) are inverse bijections and preserve factorization multiplicities.
- Consecutive faces share exactly one residue coordinate.
- The telescope correctly eliminates \(V_1,\ldots,V_k\) without retaining dependence on the next vertex; the final anchored sum is exactly (T1) with \(c=1\).
- Dividing by \((q-1)^kq^{\sum(d_j-1)}\) gives precisely the product in (JC), so the asserted shape-event independence is valid.
- Apart from the missing O2 allocation, the seven indexed row families are sufficiently explicit finite mathematical families; their grammar annotations are correct.
- The lower-block induction is noncircular, and all listed operations stay in \(\mathcal R\).
- The determinant reductions, gcd calculation, margins, base changes, and solve algebra are correct.
- No argument imposes a restriction on characteristic, tameness, or sufficiently large \(q\).

Because the statement includes both the underdefined general O2 family and the unsupported concrete degree-3-table conjunct, the full claim does not follow.

VERDICT: UNSOUND
